intro: Before you stands Döner Kümbet, a tomb in Kayseri province, built c. 1276 for Şah Cihan Hatun. Walk slowly around its twelve sides. Its conical cap and its bands of tree-of-life, double-headed eagle and lion reliefs have made it the emblem of Seljuk funerary architecture.
history: Built around 1276 for Şah Cihan Hatun, this is the best known of Kayseri's Seljuk tomb towers. Its twelve-sided body and conical cap give it its name: as you walk around it, the building seems to turn. Beneath your feet, the burial chamber is kept separate from the prayer room inside the shaft.
highlights: As you wander around the tomb, don't miss the conical cap, the tree of life relief, the double-headed eagle and the lion figures, and finally the crypt below.
facts: Did you know? The double-headed eagle on its shaft was a Seljuk dynastic emblem, a device that would turn up centuries later on European coats of arms. And no, the tomb does not really turn: the name comes from the way the twelve-sided shaft seems to rotate as you walk around it. The animals facing each other across the tree-of-life relief continue a decorative tradition carried all the way from Central Asia.
outro: This brings our journey around Döner Kümbet to an end. Please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. This tomb has kept its quiet watch for centuries; let it keep watching over those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
